name: pn532
title: Driver of the NXP PN532
source: UM0701-02 Rev. 02, PN532 user manual for firmware V1.6, NXP document 141520

severity.high: with a working chip and ordinary use of a public function, the program corrupts memory, hangs, returns wrong data or a false success, or the function cannot work at all. Data from a card or a chip counts as ordinary input whatever its length: a card can hold anything.
severity.medium: the same, but only after a fault (a dead chip, a lost card, a bus error), at a limit of a legal input from the application, or in a configuration the library offers and does not use by default.
severity.low: a leak on an error path, an unchecked call with no harm in ordinary use, a text that disagrees with the code.

i2c.text: talks to the chip over I2C (6.2.4): address 0x48 on the wire, 0x24 in 7 bits, up to 400 kHz. A status byte comes first in each read. After NOT READY the host sends STOP and tries again. A ready frame is read whole before STOP, or its remaining bytes are lost.

spi.text: talks over SPI (6.1.1.1, 6.2.5): mode 0, LSB first, up to 5 MHz. The first byte says what follows: 0x02 status read, 0x01 data write, 0x03 data read.

uart.text: talks over HSU, the serial link (6.2.3).

esp_idf.text: compiles under ESP-IDF with no Arduino layer. Note which driver API it calls (driver/i2c_master.h or the old driver/i2c.h, spi_master, uart).

esp_idf_component.text: has an idf_component.yml or a CMakeLists.txt with idf_component_register.

ack_checked.text: reads the ACK frame after a command and acts when it is missing: on an LCS or DCS error the chip sends nothing (6.2.2.1 b). The chip never sends a NACK (6.2.1.4).

nack_resend.text: on a bad or missing response, sends a NACK frame to get the last response again (6.2.2.1 c).

checksums_checked.text: verifies LCS and DCS of a response.

extended_frames.text: handles the extended frame, which the chip uses above 255 bytes, up to 265 with TFI (6.2.1.2).

error_frame.text: recognizes the syntax error frame 00 00 FF 01 FF 7F 81 00 (6.2.1.5).

response_code_checked.text: checks that a response carries TFI D5 and the command code + 1.

status_decoded.text: takes the error code from bits 5..0 of the Status byte, apart from MI in bit 6 and NAD in bit 7 (7.1).

irq.text: can wait on the P70_IRQ line (6.1.2, 6.2.4.2, 6.2.5.2).

ready_polling.text: polls the ready status (the status byte on SPI and I2C).

bounded_waits.text: every wait for the chip has a timeout, so a dead chip cannot hang the program.

abort_on_timeout.text: a wait the host gives up ends with an ACK frame, which aborts the command (6.2.2.1 d, 6.2.2.2 b). MxRtyPassiveActivation is 0xFF by default, so without a card InListPassiveTarget does not end by itself (7.3.1).

nonblocking_detect.text: can start a passive detection and collect the result later, without blocking.

iso14443a_uid.text: reads the UID of a type A card (InListPassiveTarget, BrTy 0x00, 7.3.5).

two_targets.text: asks for and handles MaxTg = 2, the limit for type A.

mifare_classic.text: authenticates and reads or writes blocks.

iso14443_4_apdu.text: exchanges APDUs with a card (InDataExchange on ISO-DEP), as DESFire needs.

chaining.text: handles the MI bit, for data that does not fit one exchange (7.3.8, 7.4.5).

card_emulation.text: TgInitAsTarget and the commands after it (7.3.14).

rf_field_control.text: RFConfiguration CfgItem 0x01, the field on and off (7.3.1).

reset_recovery.text: can recover a chip that stopped answering, by a reset line or by starting over.

several_readers.text: two readers can work in one program: no state of one reader lives in a global or static.

shared_spi_bus.text: two readers can share one SPI bus with a chip select each.

thread_safety.text: a lock or a stated rule for use from several tasks.

errors_returned.text: a failure reaches the caller as a value it can tell apart.

buffers_bounded.text: lengths from the chip or the card are checked before they are copied into a buffer.

allocation_checked.text: where memory is allocated, a failed allocation is handled.

tests.text: tests that run without or with hardware.

docs.text: a README or API text that says how to use it.
